Louisiana: 26 held tree records · 18 research locations

All records identify Taiwan flowering cherry (Prunus campanulata); cultivars are unspecified. No public viewing position is established. None lies inside the three park-boundary layers checked. Nearby trees share a research group, while their distinct source IDs are retained. The closest returned city sidewalk is 34.6 m away. A sidewalk more than 10 m away needs additional sight-line evidence before inclusion; distance alone does not prove visibility.

Distances below use the current city sidewalk layer in 100 m search windows. A blank match does not prove a sidewalk is absent. Database updates and the state's 2025 migration records are not new field observations. Download all 26 decisions and coordinates ↓

Research snapshot: 27 October 2026. This catalogue is not exhaustive. Park inventory points are checked against public park polygons; the High Plains collection is checked against its published visitor map. Streetside entries use agency classifications and nearby mapped sidewalks. The 14 Iowa walks with historical access labels use planting-strip records (2011–2022) interpreted with DNR’s field protocol; current sidewalks and tree survival are unverified. For all streetside entries, viewing access is inferred and excludes private-property entry. Maine’s orchard requires a reservation. Counts describe accepted records, not complete collections. Dates and source status appear in site details; current survival needs field checks. Pink does not indicate current bloom. Bloom observations, viewing windows and forecasts remain separate. Tree data: Montgomery Parks / M-NCPPC, Lincoln, Burlington, Lawrence, Iowa DNR, East Baton Rouge, Sioux Falls and High Plains Arboretum. Garden records include Sharlot Hall Museum and University of Nevada, Reno. Base geometry: US Atlas / U.S. Census. Park and garden boundaries, sidewalk evidence, and some coordinates: © OpenStreetMap contributors.
